intro: Four very common words that do not behave like their English partners.
p.otro.nota: It agrees with the noun. In general modern Spanish, use otro/otra without un/una.
p.mismo.nota: It agrees with the noun: mismo, misma, mismos, mismas.
b1.texto:
With a noun meaning the whole of something, **todo/toda/todos/todas** commonly appears with a definite article: **todo el** día, **toda la** casa, **todos los** días, **todas las** semanas. Other patterns have no article: **todo mi tiempo**, **toda esta semana**. Used alone, **todo** can mean everything: lo sé **todo**.

**Todo el mundo** means everybody and takes a singular verb: todo el mundo **está** aquí.

**Otro/otra/otros/otras** agrees with the noun and normally takes no un/una before it: quiero **otro** café; **otra** vez; **otros dos** cafés. **Cada** does not change and takes a singular noun: cada día, cada semana, cada uno. **Algunos/as** means some; **varios/as**, several; **los demás**, the others or the rest.

**Mismo/misma/mismos/mismas** means the same and agrees with the noun: **el mismo** café, **la misma** tostada. With neuter **lo**, **lo mismo** means the same thing: siempre pido **lo mismo**.
b2.f2: I come here every day. I know everybody.
b2.f3: And do you always order the same thing?
b2.f4: Yes. Every morning, a coffee and a piece of toast.
b2.f5: Some days you can try something else. Everyone else does.
b4.o1.refuerzo: This is not the usual form in general modern Spanish; say otro café.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Cada takes a singular noun with no article: cada día.
b6.pregunta: Complete: each day I study for an hour.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Otros días would be other days.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Todo el mundo takes a singular verb.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The verb is third person singular.
b9.traduccion: I always order the same thing.
b10.pregunta: Complete: I order the same piece of toast.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Mismo agrees with the feminine noun tostada.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (60–80 words).** Write about your habits using todos los días, cada semana, otro, el mismo, todo el…

**Speak (about 1 minute).** Say aloud what you do every day, every week and every year, and what you would like to change for something else.
